question.problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $u$ and $v$ are orthogonal. Find $(2u+3w)\cdot v+u\cdot (v-w).$
question.worked_solution:
Since $u$ and $v$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that $u\cdot v=0.$ Therefore, using linearity of the dot product to expand the parentheses, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(2u+3w)\cdot v+u\cdot (v-w) & =(2u)\cdot v+(3w)\cdot v+u\cdot v-u\cdot w \\  & =2(u\cdot v)+3(w\cdot v)+u\cdot v-u\cdot w \\  & =0+3(w\cdot v)+0-u\cdot w \\  & =3(w\cdot v)-u\cdot w \\  & =3(0\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 2+(-3)\cdot 0+(-2)\cdot 1) \\  & -(0\cdot 0+(-1)\cdot 1+3\cdot (-3)+2\cdot (-2)) \\  & =3(0+2+0+-2)-(0-1-9-4) \\  & =0-(-14) \\  & =14.\end{aligned}
$$
